Definition: Rahab (i.e. boaster), an epithet of Egypt
BiblicalUsage: Rahab is the boaster — an epithet of Egypt, the proud sea-monster. Isaiah cries, 'Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD... Art thou not it that hath cut Rahab, and wounded the dragon?'; the psalm says God will make mention of Rahab and Babylon among those that know Him; and again, 'Thou hast broken Rahab in pieces, as one that is slain.'
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Rahab is Egypt with its mask off: the boaster that God cut in pieces at the sea, and yet the psalm says He will count Rahab among those who know Him — judgment and welcome in the same name.
